presets.name: BO6 Original
presets.desc: THE BASELINE. Field verdict: "the most stable I have had" — every game’s Baseline card below is this exact build with only the sens number changed, except Rivals (Y/X 0.85), The Finals (78.95cm/360) and each game’s own filter plan. 57 px/mm, classic curve accel 0.105 / cap 3.6 / input offset 0.5 (driver formula 1+a(v−off)²/v), Y/X 0.789, snap 9°, reset 80, HDL 87 + the CoD Master vertical recoil rail (T1, flicks bit-exact). Your own numbers pin the base: sens 14.70 at 250 DPI = 37.70cm/360 — for BO6/BO7 type 2.54, pair with MDC 1.33 + Relative + Affected, FOV 120 (max) (~147.8° at 5120×1440, verified hor+ model). Measured: micro-aim 99% below the 8.8mm/s offset, 180 in 58.4mm at 150ms, accel_eff 5.98, cap at 452mm/s. The sim scores its hold at −18.5% and the field overruled it — stability here comes from the slow 37.70cm base plus a perfectly CONTINUOUS ramp (no knees, no gear boundaries: drift is trainable, flips are not). That finding is now the design law of this roster.

presets.name: Breakpoint
presets.desc: The snappiest of the three Breakpoint cards — and its flicks land MORE consistently than the Baseline. Same DNA as BO6 (57px/mm, cm 37.70, offset 8.8mm/s, one continuous ramp, snap 9°), pushed to accel 0.246 (accel_eff 14) / cap 5.0. The design discovery: the cap saturates by 303mm/s — below committed flick speed — so every real flick rides the flat cap and consistency rises WITH snap: measured committed spread 13.3% vs Baseline 30.7%, 180 in 41.0mm at 150ms and 37.7mm at full commit, micro 99% and 5.6 ms (two reports) onset byte-identical to BO6. This achieves what the retired gear-shift cards attempted, with zero gain discontinuity. How to play it (two-phase): THROW committed — the cap rewards speed and a lazy 200ms flick rides the ramp and lands short; then SETTLE below 8.8mm/s where the curve is pure 1:1 — one throw, one slow correction, never a second fast chase. The honest price: tracking reads 2.45x at 120mm/s — this is a duel/entry/flick card, not a tracking card; use a game quad for sustained-track days. Game sens numbers unchanged (same 37.70cm). Measured next step: eff 16 at cap 5.0 (the Holdfast Sabre curve) = 38.8mm 180 and 9.1% committed spread at 2.65x tracking — the intensity dial above 50 walks accel toward it (and raises the cap too).

presets.name: Breakpoint Wide
presets.desc: Breakpoint at the speed you actually play The Finals. Identical DNA to Breakpoint - same 57px/mm, same snap 9°, same classic accel 0.246 / cap 5.0 / offset 0.5, same unity pocket to 8.8mm/s - with ONE change: the base is authored at cm/360 78.95 instead of 37.70. That number is not theory. On 2026-09-10 you played The Finals at Mouse Look Sensitivity 8 on this rig and rated it good; 8 at 57px/mm IS 78.95cm/360 once the Finals constant is right (ev-20260910-finals-k - the old K was a copy of Overwatch’s and read 6.6x low). What it feels like: every distance at the same pen speed scales by 2.09x against Breakpoint - the slow base is twice as long, so micro-corrections and held tracking are far calmer, and because the cap is still 5.0 the flick end lands at ~15.8cm/360 instead of ~7.5cm. The two-phase play is unchanged: THROW committed so the flick rides the flat cap, then SETTLE under 8.8mm/s where the curve is pure 1:1. Why it is a separate card: cm/360 sets the recommended sens for EVERY game at once, so this speed could not be folded into Breakpoint without halving the recommendation for CoD, Rivals, Apex, OW2, Holdfast, Valorant and HD2. Keep Breakpoint for the BO6-derived 37.70 world and use this when you want that same flick character on a long, calm base. Measured against Breakpoint on the same rig: onset 5.6 ms (two reports), micro 99% and skid 0.389mm are BYTE-IDENTICAL - the curve is the curve - and the only number that moves is the 180, 41.0mm → 78.95mm at 150ms, which is the long base at work and exactly the point of the card.

presets.name: Breakpoint Slow Center
presets.desc: Breakpoint with the center dialed in — v2, after your field verdict. The first version used a 0.90 floor to calm the center: it measured free on the old harness (same onset, same micro) but you called it “kinda high latency feeling” — the second time in this project a sub-unity floor has produced that feeling despite clean numbers. Retired. v2 keeps the floor at EXACTLY 1.00 and dials the center in the latency-free way: the unity pocket widens from 8.8 to 12.3mm/s (offset 0.7), so the first 12mm/s of every micro-correction is arithmetically 1:1 with more room before acceleration bites. The rest of the curve is Breakpoint: eff 14 to cap 5.0, saturating at 309mm/s — measured 180 in 41.5mm, committed spread 14.9%, micro 99%, onset 5.6 ms (two reports). Classic-authored now (no LUT). The calm-hold number the old floor bought is gone — your hands said it cost more than it paid.

In game: set the Psylocke hero-specific sensitivity to 1.06; mouse acceleration and mouse smoothing OFF; NVIDIA Reflex ON; dynamic resolution OFF.

presets.name: Master Preset
presets.desc: THE MASTER PRESET — everything this project has proven, in one card. Synthesis of the deep dives: the mouse RawAccel community consensus (low-sens base + accel for flicks, offset above the precision band) is your BO6 law arrived at independently; osu wisdom (area as big as comfortable, accuracy from the fingers) backs the 57px/mm grid; and our own measured history supplies the parts: the 37.70cm base, a unity pocket to 12.3mm/s (floor exactly 1.00 — the earlier 0.90 floor measured free but FELT like latency; retired by field verdict), one continuous ramp (drift is trainable, flips are not), micro 99% and 5.6 ms (two reports) onset on every unity-floor card, and the pressure-gated Tap Anchor pin — bit-exact off the click, the one filter that survived every era. One-taps ARE committed flicks, so this master runs the Breakpoint discovery at discipline strength: eff 12 saturating at 265mm/s puts every committed flick on the flat cap — committed flick spread 8.2%, the tightest of the seven Master Presets — and the 45ms pin rides through the counter-strafe click. Vanguard rules: real mouse untouched, fire on a keyboard key via pen tip. 180 in 47.1mm, tracking 2.28x (rare in this game), pin 45ms/0.6mm. In-game sens 0.239.

presets.name: Baseline
presets.desc: BO6 verbatim at Valorant sens — the field-proven physics, untouched. Classic accel 0.105 / cap 3.6 / offset 0.5: micro 99% below 8.8mm/s, tracking 1.62x, 180 in 58.4mm at 150ms. Type 0.239 in game. Vanguard rules: never touch the real mouse from launch to match end; fire stays on a keyboard key mapped to the pen tip.

presets.name: Planted
presets.desc: The baseline, calmed: accel 0.075 / cap 2.6 / offset 0.7. Same 37.70cm base, same 99% micro — but the 1:1 band widens to 12.3mm/s, tracking eases to 1.41x, committed flick spread drops 30.7% → 21.8%. 180 at 72.5mm. The discipline pick: cap 2.6 makes a panicked wide swing much harder to produce — arguably the right Valorant default. Ships the Valorant Lab filter ON (a 0.05 EMA, T3 — the only Valorant card above T1); measured through it, micro stays 99% and onset 5.6 ms (two reports). Same in-game sens as Baseline (0.239).

presets.name: Turbo
presets.desc: The baseline, heated: accel 0.14 / cap 4.5 (offset unchanged). Same low end and 99% micro; tracking 1.82x and a 180 in 52.0mm at 150ms — shorter at full commit. The honest costs: hotter mid-track gain than Baseline/Planted/Tapped and committed flick spread 34.2%. Cap 4.5 in a one-tap game is spicy — for operator repositioning styles only. Same in-game sens as Baseline (0.239).

presets.name: Tapped
presets.desc: The baseline plus the click pin: Tap Anchor 45ms / 0.6mm, exact-passthrough (hold 0 — zero added latency at all times, only the pressure-gated pin runs). Pin rides through the counter-strafe click so the shot leaves a pinned crosshair. Curve and sens identical to Baseline (0.239). Needs the plugin enabled in OTD.

presets.name: Jiggle
presets.desc: LOW-LATENCY BREAKPOINT — design principle: A PEEK CORRECTION IS RAW INPUT. Acceleration begins at 149.1mm/s: every jiggle-peek micro-correction and re-peek adjust is arithmetically 1:1 (drift 0.0), with eff 18 to 4.0 above for the wide swing. Flicks are the price: committed flick spread 59.8% and 99.2% on lazy/hesitant flicks, both the widest in the Valorant group — the 4.0 cap is not reached until 411mm/s, so committing does not fix it. Helps hardest at: shoulder-peek information play where the correction after the peek IS the kill. The LL contract: floor exactly 1.00 (the 0.90 slow-center floor measured free but FELT like latency — field verdict honored), unity center below the offset, 5.6 ms (two reports) onset, nothing above T1. 180 in 55.6mm. Sens 0.239.
